newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks continue slide on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks continue slide on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed lower for the second day in a row on Tuesday, as investors continued to take profits in light trading after last week's string of record gains.
"It's profit-taking, and overdue at that, after last week's gains. There's been no change in market fundamentals," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 33.30 points, or 0.75 percent, at 4,403.45.

In the broader market, decliners outpaced gainers by 58 to 33 out of a total of 114 shares traded. About 154.3 million shares changed hands, although dealers noted that two cross trades alone accounted for 51 million of that total.
"A little dull today after last week's excitement, but we still like the look of the market," a desk trader said.
The IPC had reached as high as 4,454.83 in early trading on what dealers said was a short-lived reaction to gains on Wall Street. Beginning in midmorning, the market declined steadily.
Analysts said inflation data released in late trading had little impact on the market.
"The inflation figures were much as expected, a little high maybe, and did nothing other than provide support at 4,400 points," said an analyst, who asked not to be named.
Banco de Mexico announced the consumer price index had risen by 0.49 percent during June 1-15. A Reuters survey of 13 financial houses showed they had forecast an average rise of 0.47 percent.
Analysts said the market failed to match a sharp recovery on Wall Street because profit-taking was overdue.
"It was healthy profit-taking, the market had not really adjusted since last week -- yesterday's decline was restrained," an analyst said.
The Dow Jones industrial average, meanwhile, ended up 153.80 percent at 7,758.06.

Dealers said Telmex L shares weighed most heavily on the market and mirrored broad market behaviour, by ending off 14 centavos (2 cents) at 19.00 pesos ($2.39), after hitting a session high of 19.24 pesos ($2.42).
Financial group Bancomer B shares ended off 3 centavos (less than 1 cent) at 3.89 pesos (49 cents) after brisk trade, after reaching a year high of 4.01 pesos (51 cents) in early dealing.
The two stock series accounted for about one-quarter of all shares traded during the session, not counting cross trades.
Retail chain Controladora Comercial Mexicana was the most heavily traded gainer, up 10 centavos (1 cent) to 7.26 pesos (91 cents).
Traders said the stock gained on revaluation by foreign investors, and because it had lagged behind recent market gains.
"Those stocks that gained had lagged the market, like Grupo Corvi," an analyst said.
Food company Grupo Corvi ended up 19 centavos (2 cents) at 4.34 pesos (55 cents), and was near the head of the prominent percentage gainers' list.
